name: The prince of Tyre
charge: Saying, I am a God, I sit in the seat of God, in the midst of the seas; setting his heart as the heart of God because of the riches gotten by his wisdom and his traffick
summary: The word came to Ezekiel for the prince of Tyre, whose heart was lifted up by the riches his wisdom and trade had gathered, so that he said he was a god sitting in the seat of God in the midst of the seas, though he was a man and not God (Ezekiel 28:1-5). The Lord would bring strangers, the terrible of the nations, to bring him down to the pit, and he would die the deaths of the uncircumcised (Ezekiel 28:6-10). The classes read Tyre as the historical city in Lebanon and, as a similitude, as Edom and America (Hosea 12:10).
offenseFull: The prince of Tyre said he was a god and sat in the seat of God in the midst of the seas, yet he was a man and not God, though he set his heart as the heart of God (Ezekiel 28:2). The class reads it as a metaphor for Edom, for America: no other nation did what America has done in the midst of the seas. Another class shows how both readings stand: God speaks in similitudes (Hosea 12:10), naming a country that did exist while speaking of another, and Tyre was a city in Lebanon; the same class of 2026-04-11 reads Tyre and Zidon in Joel and Amos as the Canaanite cities that sold Judah to the Grecians (Joel 3:4-6; Amos 1:9). The seat of God, the class says, is space and rulership, the superpower sitting among the nations like the woman who sits on many waters (Revelation 17:1). A man and not God: made of dust, water and blood, whatever the crown and seal; the classes set it beside the man of Isaiah 14 and the number of a man (Isaiah 14:16; Revelation 13:18).

He was wiser than Daniel, and no secret could be hidden from him (Ezekiel 28:3). Everything you type on these devices is recorded, the class says, and will be used against you; if you entertain secret sins on your phone, he sees it. By wisdom and by his traffic, which is trade, he gathered gold and silver into his treasures, and his heart was lifted up because of his riches (Ezekiel 28:4-5). The classes give the record: treaties with the Native nations broken the minute gold was found, the forts set where the gold is, the riches of the slave trade, Haiti made to take American rice until it depended on it, and the lending of the IMF and World Bank. You read this and it sounds profound, the class says, but it is all in the negative. One teacher reads a commentary that calls it the insanity of prosperity, pride begotten of great prosperity, and carries it from Sennacherib, Nebuchadnezzar, Pharaoh and Herod to America (Acts 12:21-23).

The same spirit said Aha against Jerusalem, the gate of the peoples, expecting to grow rich from her ruin (Ezekiel 26:2); the study note says Tyre saw our loss as her come-up. The lamentation over the king of Tyre says his heart was lifted up by his beauty and he was filled with violence by the multitude of his merchandise (Ezekiel 28:16-17). Two teachings read the king of Tyre in Eden as Cain, with the harps and pipes of Jubal’s line (Genesis 4:21), and the anointed cherub that covers as the cherub set east of Eden to keep the way of the tree of life (Genesis 3:24): today that cherub is Esau, Cain again, covering the truth that we are the Israelites and whitewashing history (Ezekiel 28:13-14).
judgmentFull: Because he set his heart as the heart of God, the Lord would bring strangers, the terrible of the nations, to draw their swords against the beauty of his wisdom and bring him down to the pit, and he would die the deaths of those slain in the midst of the seas (Ezekiel 28:6-8). The classes read the terrible of the nations as the terrorists of the nations, and the strangers as his own allies turning on him. Would he still say he was God before the one who slew him? He would be a man and not God in the hand of the one who killed him (Ezekiel 28:9-10).

Against the city, the Lord would bring many nations up like the waves of the sea and make her a bare rock for spreading nets, and He brought Nebuchadnezzar from the north as His sword against a nation that gained from our fall (Ezekiel 26:3-12). At her fall the princes of the sea would come down from their thrones and lament the renowned city of seafaring men (Ezekiel 26:15-18), and the study note sets beside it the shipmasters and sailors standing afar off at the burning of the great city, the seafaring city that reflects Esau’s nation (Revelation 18:17-19; Isaiah 14:12). She would be sought and never found again, the note says, because she said Aha (Ezekiel 26:21). The king of Tyre was cast out of the mountain of God as profane, which one teaching reads as cast out of Israel’s homeland, and fire from his own midst brought him to ashes before all who saw him (Ezekiel 28:16-19).

lawsResolved.text: Pride and arrogance brings decline, punishment and destruction.
A haughty heart leads to destruction.
There is but one God, the LORD God the Father.
Punishment will come to those who attempt to gain by deceit.
Do not glory or trust in your riches.

text.text: The word of the Lord came again unto me, saying,

Son of man, say unto the prince of Tyrus, Thus saith the Lord God; Because thine heart is lifted up, and thou hast said, I am a God, I sit in the seat of God, in the midst of the seas; yet thou art a man, and not God, though thou set thine heart as the heart of God:
Behold, thou art wiser than Daniel; there is no secret that they can hide from thee:
With thy wisdom and with thine understanding thou hast gotten thee riches, and hast gotten gold and silver into thy treasures:
By thy great wisdom and by thy traffick hast thou increased thy riches, and thine heart is lifted up because of thy riches:
Therefore thus saith the Lord God; Because thou hast set thine heart as the heart of God;
Behold, therefore I will bring strangers upon thee, the terrible of the nations: and they shall draw their swords against the beauty of thy wisdom, and they shall defile thy brightness.
They shall bring thee down to the pit, and thou shalt die the deaths of them that are slain in the midst of the seas.
Wilt thou yet say before him that slayeth thee, I am God? but thou shalt be a man, and no God, in the hand of him that slayeth thee.
Thou shalt die the deaths of the uncircumcised by the hand of strangers: for I have spoken it, saith the Lord God.
I have also spoken by the prophets, and I have multiplied visions, and used similitudes, by the ministry of the prophets.

Son of man, say unto the prince of Tyrus, Thus saith the Lord God; Because thine heart is lifted up, and thou hast said, I am a God, I sit in the seat of God, in the midst of the seas; yet thou art a man, and not God, though thou set thine heart as the heart of God:

Yea, and what have ye to do with me, O Tyre, and Zidon, and all the coasts of Palestine? will ye render me a recompence? and if ye recompense me, swiftly and speedily will I return your recompence upon your own head;
Because ye have taken my silver and my gold, and have carried into your temples my goodly pleasant things:
The children also of Judah and the children of Jerusalem have ye sold unto the Grecians, that ye might remove them far from their border.

Thus saith the Lord; For three transgressions of Tyrus, and for four, I will not turn away the punishment thereof; because they delivered up the whole captivity to Edom, and remembered not the brotherly covenant:
And there came one of the seven angels which had the seven vials, and talked with me, saying unto me, Come hither; I will shew unto thee the judgment of the great whore that sitteth upon many waters:
They that see thee shall narrowly look upon thee, and consider thee, saying, Is this the man that made the earth to tremble, that did shake kingdoms;
Here is wisdom. Let him that hath understanding count the number of the beast: for it is the number of a man; and his number is Six hundred threescore and six.
Behold, thou art wiser than Daniel; there is no secret that they can hide from thee:
With thy wisdom and with thine understanding thou hast gotten thee riches, and hast gotten gold and silver into thy treasures:
By thy great wisdom and by thy traffick hast thou increased thy riches, and thine heart is lifted up because of thy riches:
And upon a set day Herod, arrayed in royal apparel, sat upon his throne, and made an oration unto them.
And the people gave a shout, saying, It is the voice of a god, and not of a man.
And immediately the angel of the Lord smote him, because he gave not God the glory: and he was eaten of worms, and gave up the ghost.
Son of man, because that Tyrus hath said against Jerusalem, Aha, she is broken that was the gates of the people: she is turned unto me: I shall be replenished, now she is laid waste:

By the multitude of thy merchandise they have filled the midst of thee with violence, and thou hast sinned: therefore I will cast thee as profane out of the mountain of God: and I will destroy thee, O covering cherub, from the midst of the stones of fire.
Thine heart was lifted up because of thy beauty, thou hast corrupted thy wisdom by reason of thy brightness: I will cast thee to the ground, I will lay thee before kings, that they may behold thee.
And his brother’s name was Jubal: he was the father of all such as handle the harp and organ.
So he drove out the man; and he placed at the east of the garden of Eden Cherubims, and a flaming sword which turned every way, to keep the way of the tree of life.

Thou hast been in Eden the garden of God; every precious stone was thy covering, the sardius, topaz, and the diamond, the beryl, the onyx, and the jasper, the sapphire, the emerald, and the carbuncle, and gold: the workmanship of thy tabrets and of thy pipes was prepared in thee in the day that thou wast created.
Thou art the anointed cherub that covereth; and I have set thee so: thou wast upon the holy mountain of God; thou hast walked up and down in the midst of the stones of fire.
Therefore thus saith the Lord God; Because thou hast set thine heart as the heart of God;
Behold, therefore I will bring strangers upon thee, the terrible of the nations: and they shall draw their swords against the beauty of thy wisdom, and they shall defile thy brightness.
They shall bring thee down to the pit, and thou shalt die the deaths of them that are slain in the midst of the seas.
Wilt thou yet say before him that slayeth thee, I am God? but thou shalt be a man, and no God, in the hand of him that slayeth thee.
Thou shalt die the deaths of the uncircumcised by the hand of strangers: for I have spoken it, saith the Lord God.
Therefore thus saith the Lord God; Behold, I am against thee, O Tyrus, and will cause many nations to come up against thee, as the sea causeth his waves to come up.
And they shall destroy the walls of Tyrus, and break down her towers: I will also scrape her dust from her, and make her like the top of a rock.
It shall be a place for the spreading of nets in the midst of the sea: for I have spoken it, saith the Lord God: and it shall become a spoil to the nations.
And her daughters which are in the field shall be slain by the sword; and they shall know that I am the Lord.

For thus saith the Lord God; Behold, I will bring upon Tyrus Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon, a king of kings, from the north, with horses, and with chariots, and with horsemen, and companies, and much people.
He shall slay with the sword thy daughters in the field: and he shall make a fort against thee, and cast a mount against thee, and lift up the buckler against thee.
And he shall set engines of war against thy walls, and with his axes he shall break down thy towers.

By reason of the abundance of his horses their dust shall cover thee: thy walls shall shake at the noise of the horsemen, and of the wheels, and of the chariots, when he shall enter into thy gates, as men enter into a city wherein is made a breach.
With the hoofs of his horses shall he tread down all thy streets: he shall slay thy people by the sword, and thy strong garrisons shall go down to the ground.

And they shall make a spoil of thy riches, and make a prey of thy merchandise: and they shall break down thy walls, and destroy thy pleasant houses: and they shall lay thy stones and thy timber and thy dust in the midst of the water.
Thus saith the Lord God to Tyrus; Shall not the isles shake at the sound of thy fall, when the wounded cry, when the slaughter is made in the midst of thee?

Then all the princes of the sea shall come down from their thrones, and lay away their robes, and put off their broidered garments: they shall clothe themselves with trembling; they shall sit upon the ground, and shall tremble at every moment, and be astonished at thee.

And they shall take up a lamentation for thee, and say to thee, How art thou destroyed, that wast inhabited of seafaring men, the renowned city, which wast strong in the sea, she and her inhabitants, which cause their terror to be on all that haunt it!
Now shall the isles tremble in the day of thy fall; yea, the isles that are in the sea shall be troubled at thy departure.
For in one hour so great riches is come to nought. And every shipmaster, and all the company in ships, and sailors, and as many as trade by sea, stood afar off,
And cried when they saw the smoke of her burning, saying, What city is like unto this great city!

And they cast dust on their heads, and cried, weeping and wailing, saying, Alas, alas, that great city, wherein were made rich all that had ships in the sea by reason of her costliness! for in one hour is she made desolate.
How art thou fallen from heaven, O Lucifer, son of the morning! how art thou cut down to the ground, which didst weaken the nations!
I will make thee a terror, and thou shalt be no more: though thou be sought for, yet shalt thou never be found again, saith the Lord God.

By the multitude of thy merchandise they have filled the midst of thee with violence, and thou hast sinned: therefore I will cast thee as profane out of the mountain of God: and I will destroy thee, O covering cherub, from the midst of the stones of fire.
Thine heart was lifted up because of thy beauty, thou hast corrupted thy wisdom by reason of thy brightness: I will cast thee to the ground, I will lay thee before kings, that they may behold thee.

Thou hast defiled thy sanctuaries by the multitude of thine iniquities, by the iniquity of thy traffick; therefore will I bring forth a fire from the midst of thee, it shall devour thee, and I will bring thee to ashes upon the earth in the sight of all them that behold thee.
All they that know thee among the people shall be astonished at thee: thou shalt be a terror, and never shalt thou be any more.
